author: Asmae
title: Introduction to Computer Systems
extends: COMP101_ONTOLOGY.json (static curriculum ontology) — cross-references into it are foreign keys by ID, not duplicated locally.

entity_types.name: Lecture
entity_types.definition: A course unit defined by the curriculum with a sequence number, title, and learning outcomes. Organizational — groups content and defines ordering, doesn't itself teach anything.

entity_types.name: Concept
entity_types.definition: A pure abstract idea or theoretical principle with no runtime existence, syntax, or physical form (e.g. Scope, Layer Model, Time Complexity).

entity_types.name: DataType
entity_types.definition: A Python-level classification of values determining valid operations and storage — what type() would return.

entity_types.name: Skill
entity_types.definition: A transferable cognitive operation a student can perform across multiple unseen problems, defined by a verb phrase (e.g. "Diagnose OS-level errors by layer").

entity_types.name: Method
entity_types.definition: A callable defined on a specific Python type, accessed via dot notation.

entity_types.name: BuiltInFunction
entity_types.definition: A Python callable pre-defined in the built-in/stdlib namespace, invoked as a free function.

entity_types.name: LanguageConstruct
entity_types.definition: A syntactic keyword, statement, or structural element of Python grammar itself.

entity_types.name: ErrorType
entity_types.definition: A named Python exception class that can be raised when an operation fails (e.g. PermissionError, UnicodeDecodeError).

entity_types.name: Encoding
entity_types.definition: A defined mapping between raw byte sequences and human-readable symbols or numeric values (e.g. UTF-8, ASCII).

entity_types.name: HardwareComponent
entity_types.definition: A physical, tangible computing component at the hardware layer — consumes power, occupies physical space (e.g. CPU, RAM, CPU Register, Cache).

entity_types.name: SystemLayer
entity_types.definition: A named, autonomous software/firmware layer in the execution stack between hardware and user code, each a complete system with its own service interface (e.g. Operating System, Kernel, Python Runtime).

entity_types.name: RuntimeEntity
entity_types.definition: A concrete artifact/execution agent created at runtime, exists for a duration, has identity while it exists (e.g. Process, Thread, Bytecode).

entity_types.name: SystemMechanism
entity_types.definition: An OS/hardware operational procedure or policy the system executes automatically, enforced rather than invoked (e.g. System Call, CPU Scheduling, Virtual Memory, stdin/stdout/stderr).

entity_types.name: SystemProperty
entity_types.definition: A named, inspectable, mutable value attached to a running process or its OS environment (e.g. Process ID, Environment Variable, PATH).

relations.name: taughtIn
relations.definition: Content belongs to / is first introduced in a lecture.

relations.name: dependsOn
relations.definition: Subject cannot be meaningfully learned until the object is already understood. Prerequisite ordering between concepts/skills.

relations.name: contrastsWith
relations.definition: Subject and object are alternatives/opposites or commonly confused peers at the same level of abstraction.

relations.name: usesConcept
relations.definition: A non-Concept entity actively applies/draws on a Concept to do its work.

relations.name: producesType
relations.definition: A Method/BuiltInFunction actually yields a result of the given DataType.

relations.name: throwsError
relations.definition: Performing the subject operation can actually raise the named ErrorType under realistic conditions.

relations.name: exampleOf
relations.definition: A specific code pattern/instance concretely demonstrates a Concept or Algorithm.

relations.name: implementedBy
relations.definition: A Concept is made concrete by a mechanism/construct that realizes it.

relations.name: bestPractice
relations.definition: A recommended approach or convention associated with this entity. Datatype property, not a node.

relations.name: enables
relations.definition: Subject is a mechanism/system feature that makes the object concept/goal achievable — means-to-end, not prerequisite (contrast with dependsOn).

relations.name: partOf
relations.definition: Subject is a genuine conceptual/structural sub-component of the object.

relations.name: managedBy
relations.definition: Subject is genuinely under the runtime control/ownership of the object SystemLayer (e.g. a Process managedBy the Operating System), not just conceptually associated with it. Introduced for this ICS module — doesn't exist in OOP.

official_relations_not_used_here: PREREQUISITE_OF (no cross-lecture ordering — this module has only L11)
OPERATES_ON_TYPE (no Operator individuals in this module)
METHOD_OF (partOf is used instead — see notes)
TIME_COMPLEXITY (no Algorithm individuals in this module)
SOLVES_PROBLEM (no Algorithm individuals in this module)
notes: managedBy/manages is genuinely new to this ICS module (RuntimeEntity/SystemMechanism -> SystemLayer control edges, e.g. Process managedBy Operating System) and has no counterpart in the OOP module (comp101_L10.json) — flag during merge since it may generalize to other SystemLayer-adjacent lectures rather than staying ICS-only. Datatype annotation properties definition, courseId, cognitiveType and commonCauses are present on most individuals but aren't modeled as relations here since they're plumbing (labels/IDs), not the 15 semantic relations. isRequiredBy, isUsedBy, isProducedBy, isThrownBy and hasPart are declared purely as the OWL inverses of dependsOn/usesConcept/producesType/throwsError/partOf for reasoner symmetry, not separate semantic relations. Operator and Algorithm (2 of the official 11 entity types) have no individuals in this lecture's module — they live only in the static curriculum ontology this file extends. Unlike OOP, this module has no ImplementorType union class — implementedBy/implements range/domain directly against owl:Thing instead.
